description.p: Hold the middle mouse button and drag. The page scrolls in that direction, faster the farther you drag from where you pressed, like Windows 10 and 11. Release to stop. A quick middle click without dragging still works as a normal middle click, so paste and open-link-in-new-tab are unaffected. Diagonal drags scroll both axes, so wide pages pan too.
It works in every application, on both Wayland and X11, because it operates at the kernel input layer rather than hooking any particular desktop or toolkit.

ul.li: The speed curve is the same formula Chromium and Edge use for Windows autoscroll, so short drags crawl and long drags fly.
The cursor stays anchored at the press point while scrolling, so the scroll stays locked to the window you started in.
A toggle mode for the Windows Explorer and Firefox style: one click starts autoscroll, any click stops it.
An app blacklist that pauses midscroll over programs with their own middle-drag, such as FreeCAD, OrcaSlicer and Minecraft.
A settings window for speed, dead zone, event rate, natural scrolling and the blacklist.

description.p: This package installs a background daemon that reads mouse input devices and writes to a virtual input device. The source is small and commented, and both systemd units are sandboxed, so the code can be reviewed before you trust it.
Adds a proper software-center listing, so midscroll can be found, installed and updated from Discover and GNOME Software.

Adds a device list so you can choose exactly which devices count as a mouse, draws a ghost cursor that follows your hand while the badge stays anchored, and tightens how the daemon reads its config and hands out cursor positions.
Adds an option to enable autoscroll over the desktop and panels, off by default so a middle-drag no longer hijacks the desktop.
